title: Content Lead- Discovery
description:
You will be the editor of a machine that writes for local businesses. You will not write the content. You will decide what good means, prove whether the machine is meeting it, and find the reasons when it is not.
   

  

**About Zoca**
 Zoca builds AI agents that local service businesses hire to run the parts of the business the owner cannot get to. More than 1,000 businesses use Zoca today. We started in beauty and wellness and are backed by Accel, Elevation Capital, Better Capital and GTM Fund.
   

  

 Discovery is the agent that runs a business’s online presence: its Google Business Profile, website, service pages, blogs, Google posts and reviews. It publishes on behalf of thousands of businesses every week, many of them in the same cities.
   

  

**The terrain**
 How does content written by a machine, for a business the machine only knows through data, become genuinely useful to a person searching nearby? How does it rank, and keep ranking, when the same machine is writing for the business down the street? Nobody at Zoca owns that question today. Engineers own the pipeline. Nobody owns what comes out of it.
   

  

 You would inherit a working pipeline from keywords to topics to published pages and posts, a per\-business context layer we call Brain that holds services, staff, tone and house rules, a live connection to every business’s Google Business Profile and Search Console, every review those businesses have received, and engineers who want someone to argue with about what the pipeline should produce. Over a thousand live businesses across many cities means a natural experiment running every day, if someone reads it.
   

  

**What We Know So Far**
 Google treats content produced at volume to manipulate ranking as spam, whoever wrote it. Fluent, generic content has become free, and specific, local, useful content has not. Many businesses in the same city want the same topics. And from the outside, a page that never got indexed, a page on the wrong topic, and a badly written page all look the same.
   

  

 What we do not know, and have opinions on that we will share after we hear yours: what separates two businesses’ content in the same zip code beyond the facts about each. How much business\-specific data moves ranking compared to the prose. Which content types are worth producing at all. Where a human belongs in the loop and where a human is a bottleneck dressed up as quality. And how you know a page is good before Google tells you two months later.
   

  

**What You Would Own**
* The definition of good. A rubric a person and a model can both apply, with pages that pass, pages that fail, and why.
* The weekly read. A sample of what shipped, across cities and business types, scored against the rubric, with every failure turned into a named class rather than a one\-off fix.
* The eval set. The pages the pipeline is measured against before anything goes live, and the automated judge engineering builds from it.
* Local intent, per business type. What someone searching for a lash studio wants to read is not what someone searching for a med spa wants. You decide what we produce for each, and what we stop producing.
* The outcome numbers. Pages indexed, pages earning impressions, keywords ranked, clicks, and calls and bookings we can trace back to a page. Not output volume. Where those numbers should be is yours to argue.


 If you find yourself writing blogs, something upstream is broken, and that is the thing to fix.
   

  

**Who You Probably Are**
* You have personally made local pages rank for hundreds of small businesses, at an agency or on a marketplace, and can explain exactly what did it.
* You write well and can say precisely why a paragraph is bad, in one sentence.
* You read Search Console before you form an opinion.
* You have worked with model\-generated content and hold a view of it that is neither hype nor contempt.
* You can write a rubric, argue with an engineer about an eval, and lose the argument gracefully when the data says so.
* You have real experience with US local search, wherever you sit.


 This is not a content calendar role, a people\-management role, a brand copy role or a social media role. It reports into product, works daily with the pipeline engineers, and starts with no team.

title: Senior Copywriter
description:
Senior Copywriter — CRM, Product \& App (AI\-first)
 



 Team: Brand
 



 Works with: CRM \& Retention, Product UX, App Merchandise, CX
 



 Experience: 3\+ years
 



 Location: Indiranagar, Bangalore (In\-office)
 



  





**WHY DOES THIS ROLE EXIST?** 




 More of what we say to an existing pet parent goes out through CRM than through any campaign we’ll ever run. Push, email, in\-app, WhatsApp—it is our highest\-volume writing by a distance, and it’s the easiest place in the business for a voice to quietly go flat.
 



 It’s also where the money is. A pet parent who stays is worth more than one we win twice. Retention is a writing problem more often than anyone admits—the right words to the right cohort at the right moment, over and over.
 



 And the words don’t stop when the notification is tapped. The push lands, the app opens, and the same person now reads a home screen, a banner, an empty cart, an error, or a checkout button. If the message sounded like a friend and the app sounds like a form, we’ve lost the thread.
 



 Whoever writes the first line should have a hand in the next one.
 



 So, this role is CRM at its core, with two deliberate extensions: the product surfaces the message opens into and the app storefront it lands on.
 



  





**YOUR MISSION, SHOULD YOU CHOOSE TO ACCEPT** 




 • Think deeply about what pet parents would like, especially those who already trust us
 



 • Own every word we send an existing pet parent across push, email, in\-app and WhatsApp
 



 • Write to the cohort: new user, first order, repeat and lapsed
 



 • Map and write complete journeys across onboarding, retention, re\-engagement and win\-back
 



 • Carry the voice past the tap into onboarding screens, empty states, errors, confirmations and CTAs
 



 • Make the app storefront read like a shop someone wants to walk through, not a grid of SKUs
 



 • Test constantly, read the numbers and kill what loses—including the one you were proud of
 



 • Use AI to draft at volume, set up processes and ensure brand adherence at scale
 



 • Maintain a consistent brand personality across every channel and screen
 



 • Spot and avoid thnigs lyk thise
 



 • Collaborate with multiple internal teams to expedite the marketing team’s creative output
 



 • Create a tangible impact on the lives of pets and pet parents
 



 • Be around pets—a lot
 



  





**WHAT YOU’LL OWN** 



1. CRM \& lifecycle copy



 Every lifecycle surface—push, email, in\-app, WhatsApp and SMS. Each message should be written for the cohort and have a clear objective. A first\-time parent three days in and a subscription lapse at ninety days are not the same person and should not receive the same sentence.
 



 2\.Journeys, not sends
 



 Onboarding, retention, re\-engagement and win\-back. Map the whole arc, then write it. A brilliant one\-off inside a broken flow is still a broken flow.
 



 3\.Optimisation \& testing
 



 Own an always\-on testing calendar across subject lines, hooks, CTAs, framing and length. Read the results and act on them. Retire what underperforms instead of letting it run simply because it exists.
 



 4\.AI\-first production
 



 Generate cohort variants at volume, then edit hard. Build prompt and template systems so quality is repeatable and doesn’t live only in your head.
 



 5\.Product UX writing
 



 Own the screens our messages open into: onboarding and account setup, empty states, error and edge\-case copy, confirmations, permissions, subscription and vet\-consult flows, and button labels.
 



 The writing should be short, clear, kind and unmistakably us. You’ll work with Product UX designers inside their files and flows—not on a document thrown over the wall. When a pattern repeats, you’ll write it once and add it to the UX copy library so it stays written.
 



 6\.App merchandising \& category copy
 



 Own the storefront: home screen and banner copy, collection and category names, shelf and carousel titles, in\-app sale and campaign framing, and PDP support copy where it moves the needle.
 



 Merchandising is a weekly rhythm, not a weekly rewrite. Template recurring asks so this remains a corner of the week—not the entire week.
 



  





 Support \& service content
 



 Work with the CX team on macros, canned replies, help\-centre copy and FAQs.
 



  





**REQUIREMENTS** 




 • At least 3 years of experience in CRM, lifecycle, retention or UX copywriting
 



 • Real exposure to product or in\-app writing, even if it wasn’t part of your job title
 



 • Comfort working in Figma, inside a flow and alongside a designer
 



 • Proficiency in spoken and written English
 



 • Strong attention to punctuation, grammar and spelling
 



 • Creativity with both words and ideas
 



 • Awareness of current trends and news
 



 • An understanding of the tone required for different audiences
 



 • Experience writing for different mediums and channels, especially short\-form and character\-limited formats
 



 • Real AI fluency
 



 • An understanding of how marketing campaigns are developed, with the ability to contribute insights and words that create coherent, impactful brand campaigns
 



 • Comfort being the only writer in a room of designers, PMs and merchandisers—and holding the line on voice
 



  





 Location: Indiranagar, Bangalore

 We Are
   

  

 Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI\-powered products. We deliver industry\-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R\&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
   

  

 You Are
   

  

 You have spent years deep in semiconductor design, and you know that getting a chip to tape\-out is only half the story. The other half is making sure it can actually be tested at scale, in volume, without blowing up the schedule or the yield. You understand DFT not as a checkbox but as a discipline that makes or breaks manufacturability, and you have the hands\-on experience with scan insertion, ATPG, and tool flows to prove it.
   

  

 You are comfortable sitting across from a customer's design team, listening to their constraints, their timeline pressures, their tool frustrations, and walking out with a plan that turns those constraints into a working solution. You do not just demo tools, you configure them, script around their edges, and make them fit the problem. TCL, Python, Perl are not languages you look up, they are tools you reach for without thinking.
   

  

 You translate well. Between customer requirements and R\&D roadmaps. Between technical depth and executive summaries. Between what the tool can do today and what the customer needs by next quarter. At Synopsys, you will work on DFT solutions that shape how the industry builds and tests silicon, and the customers you support will remember the difference you made.
   

  

 What You'll Be Doing
   

  

* Work directly with semiconductor customers to understand their DFT challenges, design constraints, and tool flow requirements, then translate those into technical solutions using Synopsys DFT tools including TestMAX Manager
* Configure, customize, and deploy DFT tool flows tailored to customer designs, including scan insertion, ATPG, and verification using TestMAX ATPG, Formality, and VCS
* Deliver hands\-on technical demos and proof\-of\-concept implementations that show customers exactly how the toolset solves their specific design and test problems
* Script automation solutions in TCL, Python, or Perl to streamline customer workflows, improve tool adoption, and address gaps in existing flows
* Collaborate with Account teams to gather requirements, align on customer priorities, and provide regular technical updates throughout the engagement lifecycle
* Partner with R\&D to surface customer feedback, reproduce tool issues, and influence product roadmap decisions based on real\-world design challenges
* Stay current on DFT methodologies, semiconductor design trends, and emerging test strategies to ensure the solutions you deliver remain relevant and scalable


 The Impact You Will Have
   

  

* Enable customers to achieve faster time\-to\-market by delivering DFT solutions that reduce design iterations and improve test coverage
* Increase adoption and satisfaction with Synopsys DFT tools by making them work seamlessly within customer design environments
* Strengthen customer relationships and retention by becoming the trusted technical advisor who understands their design challenges and delivers results
* Influence the direction of Synopsys DFT product development by bringing real customer requirements and pain points directly to R\&D
* Improve silicon yield and manufacturability across the industry by helping customers implement robust, scalable DFT methodologies
* Reduce customer support escalations by proactively solving tool flow issues and building automation that prevents common failure modes
* Protect and grow Synopsys' leadership position in semiconductor design by ensuring customers see measurable value from the toolset


 What You'll Need
   

  

* Master's degree (M.Tech or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field
* 8 to 12 years of hands\-on experience in semiconductor design, DFT engineering, or related domains with direct exposure to VLSI design principles and design flows
* Deep working knowledge of Design for Testability methodologies, including scan insertion, ATPG, and DFT verification techniques
* Proficiency in scripting languages such as TCL, Python, or Perl for automation, tool customization, and workflow optimization
* Direct experience with semiconductor design tools and flows, exposure to TestMAX Manager, Formality, VCS, or TestMAX ATPG is a strong plus
* Demonstrated ability to work directly with customers, gather technical requirements, and deliver solutions that meet both technical and business objectives
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills with a track record of diagnosing complex tool or design issues and finding practical paths forward


 Who You Are
   

  

* You can walk into a customer meeting, listen to a messy design problem, and sketch out a tool flow solution on a whiteboard that makes sense to both the engineer and their manager
* You do not wait for perfect documentation or complete specs, you ask the right questions, fill in the gaps, and move forward with what you have
* You are comfortable being the bridge between customer frustration and R\&D priorities, translating "this does not work" into reproducible cases and actionable feedback
* You stay curious about what is changing in DFT, test strategies, and semiconductor design, and you bring that knowledge into the solutions you build
* You follow through, when you commit to a customer deliverable or a timeline, you make it happen or communicate early when something shifts
* You are technical enough to debug a tool flow issue yourself and collaborative enough to know when to pull in the right expert from another team


 The Team You'll Be Part Of
   

  

 You will join a team of Product Engineers and Product Specialists focused on advancing semiconductor design methodologies and delivering measurable value to customers. This team works closely with Application Engineers and R\&D to ensure customer needs are met with solutions that are reliable, scalable, and grounded in real\-world design challenges. The work you do here protects Synopsys' reputation for excellence in the semiconductor industry and directly influences how customers experience and adopt our DFT toolset.
